defaults.permitted_development: Across Hampshire, a side extension normally only falls within Class A if it is single storey, stays behind the principal elevation and does not exceed half the width of the original house. Width, parking loss and the effect of the flank wall usually decide whether it still reads as a modest addition.

rules.height_rules: Across Hampshire, the usual side-extension fallback is an overall height of up to 4m, with eaves at or below 3m where any part sits within 2m of a boundary. Keeping the side roof low is usually what stops the flank wall becoming visually heavy.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate side-extension depth allowance in the way people often expect. The real test is whether the addition stays clearly subordinate to the original house and does not turn the side elevation into an oversized new wing.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Hampshire, the key boundary checks are width, side-gap character, neighbour outlook and whether the addition creates an overbearing flank wall from the street or adjoining land.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the roof clearly secondary to the main house. A simple, low side roof is usually easier to defend than a taller form that competes with the original ridgeline.
rules.materials_rules: Materials should match or sit very closely with the existing house so the side addition reads as part of the dwelling rather than a bolt-on block.

rules.height_rules: For height, the standard fallback is still 4m overall, with the familiar 3m eaves limit applying when the side wall comes within 2m of a boundary. rules.depth_rules: Depth is judged less by a fixed metre rule than by whether the extension remains clearly subsidiary to the original side wall and does not read as an overlarge flank addition.
rules.boundary_rules: For side extensions, the boundary test is usually about width, remaining side gap and whether the new flank wall feels too assertive from next door or from the street. rules.roof_rules: The roof should stay subordinate to the house and avoid creating a bulky flank mass. On taller side work, matching roof pitch and keeping the addition back from the front are usually critical design points.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials that tie the extension back to the original house, especially on prominent flank walls that are visible from the street. On exposed coastal sites, roof profile, external finish and visual impact can carry more weight than on a routine suburban plot.

restrictions.conservation_area: If the building in Basingstoke and Deane is in a conservation area, the side addition still has to protect established gaps, visible flank elevations and the wider rhythm of the street.
